_comment: The log chunk, once, for every language.
An action narrates what it is doing on one reserved output port, whose name
no schema declares: `port` below. What travels on it is an ordinary chunk --
the payload is the logged value in whatever media type it serialised to --
carrying a timestamp and the attributes named here. Nothing about the shape
is per-language, so a Kotlin consumer reads a C++ handler's logs and a
TypeScript one reads a flow's.
The attribute keys are unprefixed, unlike `a11-close` in status_chunk.json,
because they only ever appear on this port: there is no user metadata there
to collide with, and a consumer in another language reads them as the plain
words they are.
`internal` is the one boolean, and is spelled out rather than encoded: `true`
or `false`, and absent means false. `lineno` is decimal digits. Every other
attribute is free text.
`levels` is the whole set, quietest first. A level is not a status code and
not an Abseil severity: Abseil has no debug and its fatal ends the process,
so a reporter folds `debug` onto INFO and `critical` onto ERROR while the
level written here stays exact. A consumer that can tell them apart still
can.
Each language asserts these names against this file (C++
cpp/tests/action_log_test.cc, Python a11/actions/tests/test_action_log.py,
TypeScript js/test/action_log.test.mjs, Kotlin
kotlin/src/test/kotlin/a11/ActionLogTest.kt), so a divergence fails a test
instead of a conversation.
